about.title: Temecula Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product does not care where it was bought. A space heater from a store off Winchester Road, a set of tires mounted before a run up I-15 Northbound, a child's car seat picked up near Margarita Road — any of these can fail without warning and leave a Temecula family sorting out medical bills and questions. California's approach to these cases is different from an ordinary negligence claim. Under strict liability, the focus is on the product: was there a defect in its design, in the way that particular unit was made, or in the warnings and instructions that came with it, and did that defect cause the harm? You generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. Responsibility can also reach beyond the maker to distributors and the retailer that sold it. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match people in Temecula and across Riverside County with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Temecula recorded 451 injury collisions in 2025. If a defect in my vehicle contributed to one of them, is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be. Crashes on corridors like Rancho California Road or I-15 Northbound are usually treated as driver-fault cases, but if an airbag failed to deploy, a tire separated, or a brake component gave out, a strict liability claim against the maker or seller may exist alongside any claim against another driver. Preserving the vehicle before it is repaired or scrapped is important, and an attorney can help coordinate that.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer did something wrong?
items.answer: Generally, no. Under California's strict liability rules for products, the injured person typically needs to show the product had a defect — in design, manufacturing, or its warnings — and that the defect caused the injury. Whether the company was careless is usually not the question. That said, every case turns on its facts, so an attorney should review yours.

items.question: I bought the product from a local Temecula store. Can I only go after the manufacturer?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California allows claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers in the chain of sale, which matters when the maker is overseas or hard to identify. Keep the product, any packaging, and your receipt, and let an attorney sort out who in the chain may be responsible.
